media_strategy.selection_principle: default to all five channels (chart, image, video, audio, interactive_or_map); the interactive Leaflet map is the centerpiece carrying both location and weather; charts read from analyst data_tables; real stadium photos and real climate numbers are credited

chart.reason: Quantitative rankings (feels-like, heat exposure, rain, altitude, calendar) and a temp-vs-humidity scatter are the analytical backbone.

image.reason: 15 real licensed stadium photos ground every venue; two AI atmospheric images (heat hero, hot/cool contrast) set tone and break analytical density. No fabricated stadium photos — Kansas City uses a placeholder card.

video.reason: A 6s heat-shimmer clip animates the hero so the reader sees the wavering heat rather than reading about it (image2video / veo-3.1-fast).

audio.reason: A Web-Audio sonification maps the 16 venue feels-like highs to ascending pitch, synced to the heat bar chart, plus an optional muted ambient bed; both have visual fallbacks and never autoplay.

interactive_or_map.reason: Leaflet map with 16 venues colored by heat index is the centerpiece; a 'pick a city' selector and the guess-first scatter add exploration.

media_blockers.reason: First image2video (veo-3.1-fast) attempt returned 'service experiencing high load' and failed after ~36s.
media_blockers.fallback_des: Retried once per instructions; the retry succeeded and produced heat_shimmer.mp4. No fallback to text2video or CSS was needed.

media_blockers.reason: No real photo exists in the wikimedia cache for Kansas City / Arrowhead Stadium (det_media_16).
media_blockers.attempted_command: n/a — cache had no kansas_city photo
media_blockers.fallback_des: des_14 — Kansas City rendered as a clean placeholder card (city name + climate stats + a 'no photo available' note), never a fabricated stadium image.

des_01.label: Hero: blazing stadium with heat-shimmer video

content.prompt: Slow cinematic push-in on the sun-baked stadium; heat shimmer ripples rising off the pitch, hazy amber air trembling with thermals, gentle dust motes. No camera shake, no text.

des_01.brief: Full-bleed hero: a 6-second muted, autoplay-on-view, looping clip of a packed open-air stadium baking under a white midday sun with visible heat shimmer. Headline overlays at the bottom. The still hero_heat.png is the poster/fallback. This sets the emotional thesis — heat — before a single number.
des_01.rationale: The story's emotional core is heat you can feel; subtle motion (shimmer) conveys that better than a static image, and the poster guarantees a graceful fallback.

des_02.label: Interactive Leaflet venue-climate map (CENTERPIECE)

content.initial_state: A map of North America with 16 circle markers at each venue's lat/lon. Marker color runs on a hot-to-cool ramp keyed to feels_like_c (deep red ~38C -> amber -> teal -> blue ~21C); marker radius scales with matches. A legend explains the color = feels-like and size = match count.
content.transition: A popup opens showing venue real name, city, country, match count, feels-like high, air high, humidity, rainy-day %, elevation, and a thumbnail of the real stadium photo (photo field). Kansas City shows a clean 'no photo available' placeholder in the popup instead of an image.
content.payoff: The reader sees location and weather fused: the red cluster across the southern US/Monterrey vs the cool blue of Vancouver/Seattle, and how many matches sit in each.

des_02.brief: Leaflet.js map (CDN) plotting all 16 venues from ana_09's data_table. Color = feels-like heat index, size = matches. Click a marker for a popup with full climate stats and the real stadium photo thumbnail (Kansas City: placeholder). Caption credits Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0) for climate and Wikimedia for photos. This is the single most important visual on the page.
des_02.rationale: The data is inherently geographic with lat/lon and the story is location+weather; a Leaflet map carries both dimensions at once better than any chart.

des_03.label: Feels-like ranking bar (hot->cool)

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing venue, air high, humidity, matches; play button triggers the sonification (des_07) which sweeps the bars top to bottom

des_03.brief: 16-bar horizontal ranking of average feels-like high, Houston (38.6C) at top to Vancouver (21.5C) at bottom, colored on the same hot-to-cool ramp as the map. Annotate the 17.1C spread between top and bottom. A small 'Play' control sonifies the ranking.
des_03.rationale: A sorted bar makes the 17C spread and the hot cluster instantly legible; sharing the color ramp with the map ties the two together.

des_04.label: Matches per venue bar + host-nation split

content.interaction: hover shows venue real name + country; a small inset donut/stacked bar shows the 78/13/13 nation split from ana_03

des_04.brief: Horizontal bar of matches per venue (Dallas 9 highlighted at top), colored by host nation, with a compact inset showing USA 78 / Mexico 13 / Canada 13. Sits beside a real stadium photo of AT&T Stadium (Dallas).
des_04.rationale: Shows the lopsided match load and the national split together; pairing with a real photo breaks the chart rhythm.

des_05.label: Dallas stadium photo (real, credited)

content.attribution: AT&T Stadium (Arlington) — photo by bobbyh_80, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

des_05.brief: Real photo of AT&T Stadium beside the matches-per-venue chart. Caption: 'AT&T Stadium, Arlington — 9 matches, the busiest venue and a dry-hot, climate-controlled bowl.' Credit bobbyh_80 / Wikimedia (CC BY 2.0).
des_05.rationale: Grounds the abstract '9 matches' lead venue in a real place; ties to the dry-hot + roof caveat.

des_06.label: Heat-exposure index bar (matches x feels-like)

content.interaction: hover shows matches x feels-like breakdown; an annotation band marks the FIFPRO 'extremely high risk' venues

des_06.brief: Bar of heat-exposure index (matches x feels-like), Dallas (344.7) at top. Annotate the two headline figures: 35 matches (33.7%) at feels-like >= 34C and 41 matches (39.4%) at the six FIFPRO 'extremely high risk' venues. Colored by feels-like.
des_06.rationale: Combines the two key dimensions — where the matches are AND how hot — into one ranked view that supports the lead claim.

des_07.label: Stat callouts: the headline extremes

callouts.label: feels-like high in Houston — the hottest venue
of matches at FIFPRO 'extremely high risk' venues
gap between the hottest and coolest venue

des_07.brief: Three oversized stat callouts in a row (72px numbers) drawn from ana_12 and ana_05: hottest feels-like, share of matches in the danger band, and the feels-like spread. Each with a one-line label.
des_07.rationale: These numbers are striking enough to stand alone as headline stats and pace the heat section.

des_08.label: Heat-index sonification synced to the ranking bar

content.why_audio: Hearing the 16 feels-like highs as descending tones makes the cliff from Houston's danger-zone heat down to Vancouver's mild evening audible, not just visible.
content.trigger: Click 'Play the heat ranking' below the feels-like bar chart (des_03). Never autoplays.
content.ui_form: Web Audio API generated in-browser (no asset file): each of the 16 venues maps feels_like_c to pitch (21.5C -> ~330Hz, 38.6C -> ~990Hz), 220ms per note, simple sine/triangle tone. As each tone plays, the corresponding bar in des_03 briefly highlights.
content.fallback: If Web Audio is unavailable or the reader does not click, the bar chart fully communicates the ranking; the optional ambient bed (heat_ambience.mp3) is a separate muted-by-default toggle.
content.novelty_note: Not a generic click-to-play tone card: the sonification is bound to and visibly drives the heat ranking bar, so sound and chart explain the same cliff.

des_08.brief: In-browser Web Audio sonification of the 16 venue feels-like highs (from ana_04 data_table), triggered by a button under the heat bar chart, with each tone highlighting its bar. A separate optional ambient soundscape (heat_ambience.mp3) can be toggled on as atmosphere; both are off by default.
des_08.rationale: 16 ordered values are an ideal small ranked sequence to sonify; binding it to the chart keeps it explanatory rather than decorative.

des_09.label: Ambient heat soundscape (optional bed)

content.why_audio: An optional warm shimmering drone reinforces the oppressive-heat mood of the section for readers who want atmosphere.
content.trigger: A small mute/unmute toggle in the heat section header; OFF by default, never autoplays.
content.ui_form: section-integrated mini-toggle, not a central card.

content.prompt: A short tense ambient cinematic bed evoking shimmering desert heat: sustained warm drone, distant cicada-like high shimmer, slow rising tension, no vocals, no drums, ~20s.

content.fallback: Page is fully functional silent; the toggle defaults to muted.
content.novelty_note: Used as an opt-in ambience toggle rather than a foregrounded audio player.

des_09.brief: Optional 20s ambient heat bed, off by default, toggled from the heat section. Pure atmosphere; the sonification (des_08) is the data-bound audio.
des_09.rationale: Adds tactile mood without forcing sound on the reader.

des_10.label: Climate-tribes scatter (feels-like vs humidity, guess-first)

content.initial_state: Scatter: x = humidity_pct, y = feels_like_c, bubble size = matches, point color = tribe (brutal=deep red, dry-hot=orange, warm=amber, mild=teal). A faint dividing guide at feels-like 34C and humidity 70%.
content.trigger: Reader hovers/clicks a point, or toggles tribe filters in a legend
content.transition: Hover shows city, feels-like, humidity, matches, tribe; clicking a tribe in the legend dims the others
content.payoff: The four tribes separate visually — the brutal corner (Houston/Miami/Atlanta) vs the mild corner (Vancouver/Seattle/Mexico City) — making the classification self-evident.

des_10.brief: Interactive temp-vs-humidity scatter from ana_08 with bubble = matches and color = climate tribe, filterable by tribe. Annotated with the roof/AC fairness caveat (Dallas/Houston/Atlanta climate-controlled; BC Place roof open; MetLife no roof).
des_10.rationale: A scatter is the natural way to show two climate axes at once, and letting readers filter tribes turns a static chart into exploration.

des_11.label: Hot-vs-cool contrast image (AI)

content.prompt: Split-screen diptych: left a brutally hot stadium under harsh white sun with heat shimmer; right a cool misty stadium under soft blue-grey overcast with drifting fog. Clean vertical seam. No text, no logos.

des_11.brief: Full-width AI image contrasting a sweltering venue (left) with a cool misty one (right), placed between the scatter and the rain/altitude section to visualize the brutal-vs-mild divide.
des_11.rationale: A single image makes the temperature gulf felt; breaks the chart streak between scatter and the rain chart.

des_12.label: Rain exposure bar (rainy-day share)

content.interaction: hover shows mean precip mm/day and match count

des_12.brief: Bar of rainy-day share, Miami (88%) at top to Santa Clara (0%) at bottom, colored wet-to-dry. Annotate Miami 88% and the dry California pair.
des_12.rationale: Rain is the second weather axis; a sorted bar shows the same kind of extreme spread as the heat ranking.

des_13.label: Altitude lollipop / bar

style.log_or_break_note: Mexico City 2200m and Guadalajara 1566m tower over the sea-level cluster

des_13.brief: Bar of venue elevation, Mexico City (2,200m) dominating, the rest hugging sea level. Annotate that altitude is why Mexico City stays mild despite low latitude.
des_13.rationale: Altitude is a distinct geographic dimension; the dramatic Mexico City outlier is best shown as a ranked bar.

des_14.label: Venue photo gallery (15 real photos + KC placeholder)

placeholder.note: No public-domain photo available — shown as a climate placeholder card.

des_14.brief: A responsive gallery of the 15 real licensed stadium photos, each captioned with venue name + city + its headline climate stat (feels-like / rain / altitude). Kansas City is a 16th clean placeholder card (name + stats + 'no photo available'), never a fabricated image. Every photo credited per the manifest in a Sources block.
des_14.rationale: The venues are real places; showing them makes the geography tangible and honors the real-asset-first mandate.

des_15.label: Tournament calendar timeline
des_15.brief: A timeline bar chart of matches per match-day across the 39-day window, opener (2) -> dense group stage peak (6 on 24 Jun) -> single-match knockouts -> final. Frames the closing point that dense days multiply pitches under peak afternoon heat.
des_15.rationale: Closes the loop on 'schedule meets sky' by showing when the most venues run at once.

des_16.label: Climate-not-forecast caveat callout

callouts.label: the years these climate averages are drawn from — this is typical climate for the window, NOT a 2026 forecast

des_16.brief: A distinct, visible caveat panel (not a footnote) stating the weather figures are typical historical climate (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0, 2021-2024 average) and not a forecast for any 2026 match; also notes roofs/AC mitigation and placeholder team names.
des_16.rationale: Editorial notes flag this as load-bearing honesty; it must be visible, so it gets its own callout in the close.

page_rhythm.tone: warm editorial, sun-bleached light palette with a hot-to-cool accent ramp; clean, airy, mobile-first single column with full-bleed media breaks
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first: hero video -> map centerpiece -> alternating prose, ranked bars, photos, scatter, gallery, timeline; never 3 charts in a row (photos/map/scatter/contrast image break every chart run)
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: The map is the hero rather than a chart grid; audio is a chart-bound sonification plus an opt-in ambient toggle, not a tone card; the contrast image and real-photo gallery interrupt the chart cadence; color is a single consistent hot-to-cool ramp shared between map and heat bars.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large 72px stat callouts; a clear 'CLIMATE, NOT A FORECAST' caveat panel; per-photo credits and an Open-Meteo / Wikimedia Sources block at the foot; hot-to-cool ramp legend reused across map and heat charts.
